faqs.a:
(a)
As provided in the Charter, section
4.2.1
, the city council shall have the responsibility and authority to adopt procedures
               to investigate, hear and determine violations of these rules of behavior and standards
               of conduct.
(b)
This Code shall not create any private rights of action or right to sue the city or
               individual officer or any other person.
(c)
Upon its own motion or the filing of a sworn statement with the city clerk by any
               natural person, the city council shall, cause an investigation of alleged facts, which
               if true would constitute a violation of
section 2-374
or
section 2-375
in accordance with the following provisions. Upon receipt of information as provided
               in this subsection which if true would constitute a violation of
section 2-374
and be grounds for removal from office, the city council shall either:
(1)
Refer the matter to the appropriate state, county or local law enforcement agency
               for investigation and prosecution.
(2)
Investigate the matter or refer the matter to an outside disinterested third person
               selected by the city council for investigation.
(d)
If a reasonable person would conclude based upon the investigation that it is more
               probable than not that misconduct or malfeasance has occurred then the city council
               shall:
(1)
Refer the matter to the appropriate law enforcement agency for prosecution; and/or
(2)
Direct the city attorney to initiate appropriate legal action; and/or
(3)
Refer the matter for a hearing and determination to an outside disinterested third
               person qualified to hear and determine such matters; and/or
(4)
Hear and determine the matter itself in accordance with the provisions provided in
section 2-379
.
(e)
If a reasonable person would conclude based upon results of the investigation that
               it is more probable that malfeasance or misconduct has not occurred, but that a violation
               of
section 2-375
more likely than not has occurred then the city council shall proceed to determine
               the matter as set forth below. If facts are alleged which if true would constitute
               a violation of section 2-55, the city council shall authorize such investigation using
               such means as are necessary and legal. If the results of the investigation reveal
               that it is more likely than not that a violation of
section 2-375
has occurred, the city council shall either:
(1)
Refer the matter to an outside person for investigation and determination as to whether
               the officer has violated
section 2-375
; or
(2)
Conduct a hearing in accordance with
section 2-379
to determine if the officer has violated
section 2-375
.
(f)
If the investigation reveals that is more likely than not the officer has not violated
               this Code and there is no reasonable basis for justifying further investigation, the
               allegation shall be dismissed and no further action shall be taken.
(g)
If an investigation indicates that the conduct may be criminal in nature, the matter
               shall be referred to the appropriate law enforcement authorities.
(h)
Notwithstanding city council's powers as described above, the city attorney and/or
               the city manager are authorized to directly receive allegations or complaints of any
               criminal violations of local, federal, or state law and violations of EEOC and employment
               law and are authorized to refer the allegations to the appropriate law enforcement
               or regulatory agencies for investigation. If in the best professional judgment of
               the city attorney and/or the city manager, as may be appropriate under the totality
               of the circumstances, information concerning the complaint or allegation cannot be
               revealed generally to city council without impugning the credibility or validity of
               the investigation, or otherwise destroying or revealing confidential information or
               evidence required for the investigation, then the mayor, or if the mayor is otherwise
               disqualified or unavailable, then the mayor pro tem and one other councilmember chosen
               by the mayor or mayor pro tem, shall be informed. The mayor or the mayor pro tem shall
               be authorized in such circumstance to provide direction to the city attorney and/or
               city manager until such time as city council may take action. Remaining members of
               the city council shall be informed of the matter and developments as soon as the mayor,
               city manager, and city attorney determine that the credibility or validity of the
               investigation will not be compromised by the release of the information.
(i)
No officer shall interfere with or attempt to influence any criminal, civil or administrative
               investigation performed pursuant to the Charter or this Code. To the extent consistent
               with the individual civil and legal rights of all officers, each shall have an affirmative
               responsibility to cooperate fully in any authorized investigation.
(j)
Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary, the city council may direct the city
               attorney, or if the city attorney is disqualified, the city manager, to initiate and
               prosecute any appropriate civil action for the recovery of property, a violation of
               fiduciary duty resulting in gain or any other appropriate civil action against an
               officer or employee for conduct which may also be a violation of this article.
(k)
To the applicable extent of federal and state law the city shall maintain the confidentiality
               of any records pertaining to allegations of violations of this Code and any subsequent
               investigation, and disposition.
(Code 1981, § 2-58; Ord. No. 3088, § 2, 6-27-1994)
